items.title: Abbey Lincoln — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I was singing at the Elks Club with this band, Benny Poole.

ctx.x: Was there any kind of music instruction in school? How were you learning or how were you –

I failed in music. I failed in arts. I failed in home economics. The thing that kept me in school was that I could do this performance once a year with Mr. Chinnery. I was solo singer, and I didn't know I was going to be a singer. It was just something to do. I didn't want to leave school because I didn't have anything to do and mama wouldn't want me -- she wouldn't let me just sit around and -- you know what I mean? I did it to please her. So, I finished high school, and when I was 20, going on 20, my oldest…
Do you remember what the book was was and what you were singing?
